CVE-2026-104007.title: Code execution through the JDBC driver path of a database document
CVE-2026-104007.description: LibreOffice can connect to databases through JDBC drivers written in Java. A spreadsheet can use a database as the source of a pivot table, and the database document that describes the connection names the driver to use. The location the driver was loaded from was taken from the database document itself, so a crafted document could make LibreOffice load and run Java code that the document supplied when it was opened. This is a different route to the problem fixed for CVE-2026-63277. In fixed versions the driver location is taken only from the driver configuration of the user, and a pivot table whose source is a database document named by a URL connects only once the user allows links to be updated.

CVE-2026-112255.title: Endpoint credential minting (insecure default allow-list)
CVE-2026-112255.description:
Initialization of a resource with an insecure default vulnerability in OpenText Advanced Authentication Server allows Excessive Allocation.

This issue affects Advanced Authentication Server: from 6.4.0.0 through 6.4.3.x, from 6.5.0.0 through 6.5.0.x, and from 6.6.0.0 through 6.6.1.0.

The fix for this is issue is to create a secure configuration. The 6.6.2.0 release has a best practice entry if the configuration is unsecure.

A secure configuration is to NOT allow creation/recreation of Unauthenticated Endpoints. If creation/recreation of Unauthenticated Endpoints is required, you should only allow it from trusted networks.

To remedy this issue, change your configuration to NOT allow creation/recreation of Unauthenticated Endpoints. If you require Unauthenticated Endpoints, you MUST change your configuration to use a non-empty whitelist to specify the trusted networks. An empty whitelist will allow all networks to create/recreate endpoints.

CVE-2026-131205.title: SPL Injection through Asset Center Drilldowns in Splunk Enterprise Security
CVE-2026-131205.description:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_user" Splunk Enterprise Security role could store attacker-controlled asset data in an asset source lookup. A user that holds a role with the mc_assets_read capability could later open the Asset Center dashboard and select that value in the Asset Information table. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of that user. With this access, the user who stored the asset data could expose or modify data available to the user who selected the value.
The vulnerability is possible because Asset Center does not escape asset values before adding them to drilldown searches.
The vulnerability requires Asset Center to process the asset data and another user to select the value. The user who stored the data should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.

CVE-2026-86017.title: isomorphic-git: Arbitrary File Write via Symlink
CVE-2026-86017.description: isomorphic-git is a pure JavaScript implementation of Git for Node.js and browsers. Prior to 1.38.8, git cherry-pick applies tree changes through applyTreeChanges in src/utils/walkerToTreeEntryMap.js without checking whether a leading path component is a symbolic link. If a victim worktree contains a tracked symlink to a location outside the worktree and a cherry-picked tree places a file beneath that path, the write follows the symlink and materializes attacker-controlled blob content at the external destination. This allows arbitrary file writes and can cause data tampering, code injection into interpreted files, privilege escalation, denial of service, or follow-on code execution depending on the selected target path. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.8.

The SMSC911x/LAN9220 Ethernet driver stages every outgoing frame in a fixed-size static buffer before pushing it to the controller FIFO. eth_tx() in drivers/ethernet/eth_smsc911x.c took the frame length from net_pkt_get_len(pkt) and passed it directly to net_pkt_read(pkt, tx_buf, total_len), with no comparison against the size of tx_buf (NET_ETH_MAX_FRAME_SIZE). net_pkt_read() takes no destination size and only fails when the packet is shorter than the requested length, so any packet longer than the staging buffer was copied past its end.

CVE-2026-99192.title: net: bcmgenet: unshare the skb before writing the control block
CVE-2026-99192.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: bcmgenet: unshare the skb before writing the control block

bcmgenet stores first_cb, last_cb and bytes_sent in the skb control
block and reads them back on completion to free the skb and credit BQL.
ether_setup() leaves IFF_TX_SKB_SHARING set, so the stack can resubmit
a shared skb that is still in the ring. The next transmit overwrites
last_cb, so the earlier slots complete without crediting their bytes
and BQL stalls the queue until the watchdog resets it.

Unshare the skb before writing the control block.

Reproduce with pktgen in clone_skb mode, which hands the driver the same
skb while earlier copies are still in the ring:

pg=/proc/net/pktgen
echo "add_device eth0" > $pg/kpktgend_0
echo "dst_mac AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF" > $pg/eth0
echo "dst 192.0.2.1" > $pg/eth0
echo "clone_skb 8" > $pg/eth0
echo "count 0" > $pg/eth0
echo start > $pg/pgctrl &
sleep 5
echo stop > $pg/pgctrl
wait

CVE-2026-99534.title: ksmbd: prevent stale data from being written by SMB2 WRITE requests
CVE-2026-99534.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: prevent stale data from being written by SMB2 WRITE requests

Initialize the compatibility byte in request buffers without zeroing
the entire allocation. Keep the one-byte compatibility exception for
SMB2 messages so valid zero-length WRITE requests remain compatible,
and validate the data range in the WRITE handlers against the current
compound request before accessing it.

This prevents stale request-buffer data from being written to files or
sent to IPC pipes.

CVE-2026-99659.title: mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger
CVE-2026-99659.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger

__tlb_adjust_range() takes the size of the range which has to be flushed
as an unsigned int. Its callers, tlb_flush_{pte,pmd,pud,p4d}_range(), get
and pass an unsigned long. Consequently, a range that is 4 GiB or larger
gets truncated, possibly to 0.

On arm64 with hugetlb, a 64k kernel can have 16 GiB hugetlb folios
mapped contiguously at the PMD level and flush them when unmapping, and a
16k kernel can flush 64 GiB PUDs through tlb_unshare_pmd_ptdesc(). So
at least these two scenarios are affected.

Fix it by flushing the proper range instead of the truncated one by
properly using "unsigned long" for range_size.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

scsi: target: Fix demo-mode dynamic ACL dev-entry UAF vs LUN teardown

A demo-mode (generate_node_acls=1) login that allocates a dynamic NodeACL
populates that ACL's per-LUN dev entries in core_tpg_add_node_to_devs()
*before* the ACL is linked onto tpg->acl_node_list by
target_add_node_acl():

core_tpg_check_initiator_node_acl():
...
core_tpg_add_node_to_devs(acl, tpg, NULL); /* builds deves */
target_add_node_acl(acl); /* only now listed */

The LUN teardown sweep, core_clear_lun_from_tpg(), enumerates only
tpg->acl_node_list, so a dev entry whose ACL is still in the window above
is invisible to the sweep and is never disabled. It is left on the
se_lun->lun_deve_list after core_tpg_remove_lun() frees the se_lun; when
the same unpacked_lun is later re-added and the se_lun is reallocated at
the same address, the stale dev entry is rediscovered by
target_nacl_find_deve() and core_enable_device_list_for_node()…
